title: Unbounded loop in Registry.sweep can be griefed to revert on large arrays
root_cause: Registry.sweep() iterates over the entire participants array with no pagination; once the array grows past the block gas limit, sweep() always reverts.
attacker_entrypoint: Attacker calls register() many times (permissionless) to grow participants until sweep() exceeds the block gas limit.
attacker_capabilities: call register() repeatedly from an EOA

severity_justification.worst_case: sweep() can never execute again, freezing the sweep mechanism.
severity_justification.realistic_case: Requires paying gas to register enough entries; sweep is a periodic maintenance call, not a funds path.
severity_justification.program_table_mapping: Claimed against 'protocol insolvency' (Critical) — but no funds are lost or frozen.

call_trace: Registry.sweep() -> for (i in participants) { ... }  // exceeds block gas limit and reverts

state_transition.after: participants.length = N + K (large); sweep() always reverts

asset_delta: No funds lost or frozen; sweep() (a maintenance call) becomes unavailable.
reproduction_steps: Register entries until sweep() reverts with out-of-gas
Assert sweep() reverts after the array crosses the threshold
false_positive_risks: sweep() may be callable in paginated chunks via another entrypoint (verify).
invalidating_conditions: Invalid if sweep() supports a start/end index for pagination.

defense_analysis.why_it_fails: sweep() takes no index args and always iterates the full array (contracts/Registry.sol:88).

assumptions: Attacker is willing to pay gas to inflate the array.
triager_summary: Real griefing DoS on a maintenance function, but it is claimed as Critical 'protocol insolvency' when no funds are lost or frozen. Severity is inflated; this is at most a DoS-class issue.
